issue.title: browsermcp: TestImageFromLeavesTheRest red on Windows: a Unix absolute path becomes \\work\\proj\\abs.png
issue.body:
Red on the Windows box (xiaomi-gpu, Windows 11, Go 1.26.8) in a full `go test -timeout 45m ./...` through win-run at main 373cab2b0 (2026-11-05). Windows CI only compiles the tests, so nothing else shows it (#1827). Unrelated to 373cab2b0, which changes only the Cursor mover's min string.

Package: internal/browsermcp

```
--- FAIL: TestImageFromLeavesTheRest (0.00s)
    browsermcp_test.go:211: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"x-1","method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"analyze_image","arguments":{"image":"\\work\\proj\\abs.png"}}}
         became {"id":"x-1","jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/call","params":{"arguments":{"image":"\\work\\proj\\work\\proj\\abs.png"},"name":"analyze_image"}}
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/browsermcp	0.716s
```

Not investigated: the cause. Not run: macOS or Linux (passes on CI there).

comments.body:
A test-only fix is on [the fork branch](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/5342-real-absolute-image-fixture), commit [f09fc9789](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/f09fc978998e844c834652e88f44681cc7b02796), based on ed0ab567.

The fixture constructs a drive-less Windows path (`\work\proj`), which `filepath.IsAbs` correctly treats as relative: the test was asking imageFrom to leave a relative path unchanged. It now uses `t.TempDir()` for a real absolute directory on each host. All unchanged-input cases and the relative-path rewriting assertion remain; production code is unchanged.

The browsermcp package passes race, vet and the full offline nogui build pass, and its Windows amd64 test binary cross-compiles. No Windows runner or Wine is available here; I verified the volume requirement in Go's Windows IsAbs source and used the exact failure in your report rather than claiming a native Windows run. AI-assisted implementation and review.

issue.title: gateway: persistent Azure cross-resource 400 does not fail over or cool down the failing provider

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
A persistent Azure resource-mismatch HTTP 400 ends a Smart routing-group request without trying a healthy alternative or resting the failing relay. The next client request can select the same relay again. A narrow local patch now fixes this on my Windows installation, including a naturally recurring failure after deployment.

### magpie version

Reproduced on **0.1.3545**, tag commit `6a253f8af7537e17007f39f959f55932fceaf05d`. The first locally deployed patched build was `0.1.3545-azure400.1`; the same patch has since been rebased onto v0.1.3576 as described below.

### Where / OS / setup

- Windows amd64, Magpie GUI serving the gateway; Go 1.26.8 for the local build.
- Codex using `/v1/responses` through Smart routing groups for `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`.
- Each group has an official Codex account and two custom API relays. The failing relay is called `newapi` locally; a working alternative is called `api`.
- Default/Auto affinity. The failing relay has `restCap: 720` (12 hours), not `rest-cap off`. The cap cannot help when the error never enters the rest path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a routing group with two Responses providers serving the same model, with the first eligible provider returning the exact Azure 400 below and the other returning a normal answer.
2. Send a Codex-style full-history Responses request with `store: false`, so there need not be a locally stored previous response for Magpie to repair. The attached test also covers a stored-history request whose existing repair is attempted but receives the same refusal again.
3. Inspect the routing attempts, final client status and cooldown record, then send another request through the group.

### What happened, and what I expected

Before the patch, eight group requests between 17:54 and 17:59 on 2026-11-10 (UTC+8) each tried only the failing relay, ended with HTTP 400, and had no `rest` record. The alternative was never tried. Some traces showed affinity `why: "back"`, returning from the working alternative to the earlier relay.

Expected: retain the existing bounded history repair. If this specific resource-mismatch refusal remains, try another eligible candidate before a reply reaches the client and apply the existing failure cooldown to the failing candidate. An ordinary input-validation 400 should still reach the client without failover.

### Exact upstream error

```text
The requested item was created under a different Azure OpenAI resource.
Use the same resource that created the item to access it.
```

The live response was HTTP 400 with `type: "invalid_request_error"`. Provider URLs, keys, account identities, trace IDs, conversation IDs and private request bodies are omitted.

### Cause and local fix

`prevForeign` already recognizes this refusal, and the Responses passthrough path already attempts history repair where it can. However, if repair is unavailable or still fails, `retryable` does not include this recognized 400. The group stops on that response instead of failing over and entering `restAfterMarked`.

The production change adds `prevForeign(status, raw)` to `retryable`. It reuses the existing classification and cooldown machinery; it does not introduce a new timer, discard more conversation history, or classify every 400 as retryable. A successful existing repair continues to return normally. `rest-cap off` and the existing last-candidate behavior retain their current semantics.

This concerns the remaining **failover/cooldown gap after recovery is unavailable or unsuccessful**. It is related to #4478, #5477 and #5733, but the patch does not change their history reconstruction or previous-response-pointer policies.

### Regression and executable verification

- With the new tests and the original production code, both resource-mismatch cases fail: the client gets 400, the spare is called **zero** times, and the relay is called once without stored history or three times with the first turn and failed repair included.
- With the patch, both cases pass: the spare answers, the failing attempt records a future `backoff` rest, and the next group request skips the resting relay.
- The negative-control test returns an unrelated `messages: field required` 400 and verifies no failover or cooldown.
- The existing previous-response/repair and selected retry/rest tests pass with the patch:

```sh
go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway \
  -run 'TestAzureResourceMismatch|TestPreviousResponse|TestUnknownPreviousResponse|TestNoFallbackForOtherErrors|TestRestCap|TestBackoffOneRequest' \
  -count=1 -timeout=5m
```

- An actual Windows production EXE, run with isolated configuration and local fake upstreams, serves two HTTP 200 client responses. The faulty Azure fixture is called once and the healthy spare twice; the first route records Azure 400 + `rest.by: "backoff"` followed by spare 200, and the second route uses only the spare.
- Windows `go vet -p 2 ./...`, Linux cross-vet with `-tags nogui`, the Windows default build, the Linux `nogui` cross-build and the Windows `production,comlauncher` build pass. Linux binaries were cross-built, not executed; this does not claim Linux runtime testing or a race run.

### Live verification after local deployment

The gateway was gracefully restarted onto `0.1.3545-azure400.1`, and the same real relay refusal recurred naturally. Selected fields from the routing log, with private identifiers removed:

```jsonl
{"time":"2026-11-10T18:32:36+08:00","model":"group/auto-gpt-6-1-sol","tries":[{"provider":"newapi","status":400,"rest":{"by":"backoff","failures":1,"until":"2026-11-10T18:33:56+08:00"}},{"provider":"api","status":200}],"final_status":200}
{"time":"2026-11-10T18:33:13+08:00","model":"group/auto-gpt-6-1-sol","tries":[{"provider":"api","status":200}],"final_status":200}
```

The first failed attempt carries the exact Azure error quoted above. This verifies the real Smart-group behavior in addition to the deterministic tests. The 12-hour value remains a maximum; the first failure takes the normal initial cooldown.

### Reapplied after an automatic update

During the final checks, Magpie automatically updated to official **0.1.3576**, overwriting the custom executable. I checked that tag: `retryable` still omits this resource-mismatch refusal, and `prevForeign` is unchanged. The patch applies to that version without conflicts. A rebuilt `0.1.3576-azure400.1` passed the regression and actual-EXE smoke checks again, replaced the local executable, and was activated through Magpie's own idle restart. That activation was verified, but a later automatic update to official v0.1.3577 overwrote it again despite notification-only mode. Automatic updates are now fully disabled on this installation, and the tested `0.1.3576-azure400.1` executable has been reinstalled with the official v0.1.3577 executable backed up. At the latest check, the running gateway is still `0.1.3577`; its built-in idle restart is queued while active conversations keep making requests. The binary replacement is complete, but this final reactivation is not yet confirmed.

### Full-suite status

The isolated Windows full suite on **v0.1.3545 + this patch** completed with exit code 1: **78 packages passed and 17 failed**; 9,543 top-level tests passed and 88 failed (23,488 passing and 106 failing entries when subtests are included). The new Azure tests and their subcases all passed. This is **not an all-green full-suite result**.

Known matching Windows failures include the Unix-root/symlink tests in #2425, listener-file handover tests in #5345, allocation checks in #4846, the drive-less image fixture in #5342 and the ConPTY case in #4810. Additional failures include `TestHubRootsOfACodexThread` and `TestAutoVisionDoesNotBuildListsAgain`; not every failure was independently diagnosed or fixed in this task. These failures are disclosed rather than presented as release clearance.

After the automatic update described above, the patch was applied cleanly to **v0.1.3576** (`f03ec97b8fef357a4f8baa45987ffee83151ae05`). The new regression tests, previous-response/repair tests, rest-cap tests, Windows vet, Linux cross-vet and Windows production build passed again. The actual rebuilt EXE also passed the isolated two-request smoke test (Azure called once, spare twice, two client 200s, cooldown recorded). The full suite was **not rerun on v0.1.3576**; the full-suite counts above belong to v0.1.3545.

### Patch

The patch below is based on `v0.1.3545` and includes the five-line production change, regression tests and subsystem documentation. It was produced with Codex assistance. This is a locally verified workaround and proposed upstream fix, not a claim that an official release contains it.

<details>
<summary>Unified patch — apply with git apply</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md b/docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md
index 78691a5..1ee5698 100644
--- a/docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md
+++ b/docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md
@@ -2773,8 +2773,16 @@ included). `previousResponse` in
   reproduced against Azure) is asked once more with the conversation
   whole and those ids taken out. Only a request whose conversation magpie
   holds is asked again, and only with a body that differs: an id magpie
-  doesn't hold, or a refusal with nothing of magpie's to take out, is
-  passed on as before.
+  doesn't hold, or a refusal with nothing of magpie's to take out, is not
+  sent again unchanged to that resource. If this specific resource-mismatch
+  refusal remains, `retryable` lets the next candidate answer before any
+  reply reaches the client, and the failing candidate takes its normal
+  error rest, subject to its provider's `rest-cap`. A successful repair
+  rests nobody; unrelated input-validation 400s still reach the client
+  without failover. `TestAzureResourceMismatchFailsOverAndRests` covers both
+  a failed repair and a Codex-style full-history request with `store:false`;
+  `TestAzureResourceMismatchLeavesOtherBadRequestsAlone` holds the input
+  error boundary.
 - A ChatGPT account's streamed turn goes on its conversation's kept
   socket as a delta after the backend's own `previous_response_id`
   (`codexKept`, see [Providers and accounts](providers-accounts.md)).
diff --git a/internal/gateway/azure_resource_rest_test.go b/internal/gateway/azure_resource_rest_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d04c164
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/gateway/azure_resource_rest_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,91 @@
+package gateway
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider"
+)
+
+// This is the refusal recorded by a relay serving Azure OpenAI resources.
+const azureResourceError = `{"error":{"message":"The requested item was created under a different Azure OpenAI resource. Use the same resource that created the item to access it.","type":"invalid_request_error"}}`
+
+const azureResourceAnswer = `{"id":"resp_resource","object":"response","status":"completed","output":[{"type":"message","id":"msg_resource","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"answer"}]}],"usage":{"input_tokens":3,"output_tokens":1}}`
+
+// Codex sends its own full history with store:false, so there may be no
+// stored conversation to repair. A repair that still fails has the same
+// outcome: another member answers, and later requests prefer that member
+// while the failing relay rests.
+func TestAzureResourceMismatchFailsOverAndRests(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, held := range []bool{false, true} {
+		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("stored_history=%t", held), func(t *testing.T) {
+			fresh(t)
+			up := newPrevUp(t, func(n int, _ []byte) (int, string, string) {
+				if held && n == 1 {
+					return http.StatusOK, "application/json", azureResourceAnswer
+				}
+				return http.StatusBadRequest, "application/json", azureResourceError
+			})
+			spare := newPrevUp(t, func(_ int, _ []byte) (int, string, string) {
+				return http.StatusOK, "application/json", azureResourceAnswer
+			})
+			s := prevSandbox(t, provider.Provider{ID: "azure", Name: "Azure relay", Key: "k1", Models: []string{"m1"}, Responses: up.srv.URL + "/v1", RestCap: 720})
+			if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "spare", Name: "Spare", Key: "k2", Models: []string{"m1"}, Responses: spare.srv.URL + "/v1"}); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if err := provider.SaveGroup(provider.Group{Name: "G", Members: []string{"azure/m1", "spare/m1"}, Routing: provider.Ordered, Affinity: provider.AffinityOff}); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			body := `{"model":"group/g","store":false,"input":[{"role":"user","content":"continue"}]}`
+			wantCalls := 1
+			if held {
+				id := responseID(t, askResponses(t, s, "", `{"model":"azure/m1","input":"first turn"}`))
+				body = `{"model":"group/g","previous_response_id":"` + id + `","input":"second turn"}`
+				wantCalls = 3 // first turn, then the original and repaired requests
+			}
+			rec := askResponses(t, s, "", body)
+			if rec.Code != http.StatusOK || spare.calls() != 1 || up.calls() != wantCalls {
+				t.Fatalf("client got %d, relay calls %d, spare calls %d: %s", rec.Code, up.calls(), spare.calls(), rec.Body.String())
+			}
+			route := lastRoute(s)
+			if len(route.Tries) != 2 || route.Tries[0].ID != "azure" || route.Tries[0].Status != http.StatusBadRequest || route.Tries[0].Rest == nil || route.Tries[1].ID != "spare" {
+				t.Fatalf("resource refusal did not rest and fall back: %+v", route.Tries)
+			}
+			rest := route.Tries[0].Rest
+			if rest.By != "backoff" || !rest.Until.After(time.Now()) || !strings.Contains(rest.Error, "different Azure OpenAI resource") {
+				t.Fatalf("missing cooldown or original error: %+v", rest)
+			}
+			rec = askResponses(t, s, "", `{"model":"group/g","store":false,"input":"another request"}`)
+			if rec.Code != http.StatusOK || up.calls() != wantCalls || spare.calls() != 2 {
+				t.Fatalf("resting relay asked again before spare: status %d, relay %d, spare %d", rec.Code, up.calls(), spare.calls())
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+// A normal client-input 400 must still reach the client without routing
+// the same invalid request to every provider or resting working keys.
+func TestAzureResourceMismatchLeavesOtherBadRequestsAlone(t *testing.T) {
+	fresh(t)
+	up := newPrevUp(t, func(_ int, _ []byte) (int, string, string) {
+		return http.StatusBadRequest, "application/json", `{"error":{"message":"messages: field required"}}`
+	})
+	spare := newPrevUp(t, func(_ int, _ []byte) (int, string, string) {
+		return http.StatusOK, "application/json", azureResourceAnswer
+	})
+	s := prevSandbox(t, provider.Provider{ID: "azure", Name: "Azure relay", Key: "k1", Models: []string{"m1"}, Responses: up.srv.URL + "/v1"})
+	if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "spare", Name: "Spare", Key: "k2", Models: []string{"m1"}, Responses: spare.srv.URL + "/v1"}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := provider.SaveGroup(provider.Group{Name: "G", Members: []string{"azure/m1", "spare/m1"}, Routing: provider.Ordered}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	rec := askResponses(t, s, "", `{"model":"group/g","store":false,"input":"hi"}`)
+	route := lastRoute(s)
+	if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest || up.calls() != 1 || spare.calls() != 0 || len(route.Tries) != 1 || route.Tries[0].Rest != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("ordinary bad request retried or rested: status %d, relay %d, spare %d, tries %+v", rec.Code, up.calls(), spare.calls(), route.Tries)
+	}
+}
diff --git a/internal/gateway/fallback.go b/internal/gateway/fallback.go
index 1f14e0c..feefe91 100644
--- a/internal/gateway/fallback.go
+++ b/internal/gateway/fallback.go
@@ -1919,6 +1919,11 @@ func retryable(status int, body []byte) bool {
 		return false
 	case status == 401, status == 402, status == 403, status == 404, status == 408, status == 429, status >= 500:
 		return true
+	case prevForeign(status, raw):
+		// A relay's Azure resource cannot read this history. Passthrough
+		// has already tried repairing the ids it owns; another candidate
+		// may answer, and the failing relay takes its normal error rest.
+		return true
 	case modelRetired(status, body):
 		// another provider of the model may still serve it
 		return true
```

</details>
